<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 http://maven.apache.org/maven-v4_0_0.xsd">
 <modelVersion>
  4.0.0
 </modelVersion>
 <parent>
  <groupId>
   org.sonatype.oss
  </groupId>
  <artifactId>
   oss-parent
  </artifactId>
  <version>
   7
  </version>
 </parent>
 <groupId>
  com.google.auto
 </groupId>
 <artifactId>
  auto-parent
 </artifactId>
 <packaging>
  pom
 </packaging>
 <version>
  4-SNAPSHOT
 </version>
 <name>
  Auto (Parent)
 </name>
 <description>
  A collection of code generators for Java.
 </description>
 <url>
  https://github.com/google/auto
 </url>
 <properties>
  <project.build.sourceEncoding>
   UTF-8
  </project.build.sourceEncoding>
  <java.version>
   1.6
  </java.version>
 </properties>
 <scm>
  <url>
   http://github.com/google/auto
  </url>
  <connection>
   scm:git:git://github.com/google/auto.git
  </connection>
  <developerConnection>
   scm:git:ssh://git@github.com/google/auto.git
  </developerConnection>
  <tag>
   HEAD
  </tag>
 </scm>
 <issueManagement>
  <system>
   GitHub Issues
  </system>
  <url>
   http://github.com/google/auto/issues
  </url>
 </issueManagement>
 <licenses>
  <license>
   <name>
    Apache 2.0
   </name>
   <url>
    http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0.txt
   </url>
  </license>
 </licenses>
 <organization>
  <name>
   Google, Inc.
  </name>
  <url>
   http://www.google.com
  </url>
 </organization>
 <build>
  <plugins>
   <plugin>
    <groupId>
     org.apache.maven.plugins
    </groupId>
    <artifactId>
     maven-compiler-plugin
    </artifactId>
    <version>
     3.1
    </version>
    <configuration>
     <source>
      ${java.version}
     </source>
     <target>
      ${java.version}
     </target>
     <compilerArgument>
      -Xlint:all
     </compilerArgument>
     <showWarnings>
      true
     </showWarnings>
     <showDeprecation>
      true
     </showDeprecation>
    </configuration>
   </plugin>
   <plugin>
    <groupId>
     org.apache.maven.plugins
    </groupId>
    <artifactId>
     maven-checkstyle-plugin
    </artifactId>
    <version>
     2.11
    </version>
    <configuration>
     <consoleOutput>
      true
     </consoleOutput>
     <configLocation>
      checkstyle.xml
     </configLocation>
     <failOnViolation>
      false
     </failOnViolation>
    </configuration>
   </plugin>
  </plugins>
  <pluginManagement>
   <plugins>
    <plugin>
     <artifactId>
      maven-invoker-plugin
     </artifactId>
     <version>
      1.8
     </version>
    </plugin>
   </plugins>
  </pluginManagement>
 </build>
 <profiles>
  <profile>
   <id>
    default-profile
   </id>
   <activation>
    <activeByDefault>
     true
    </activeByDefault>
    <file>
     <exists>
      ${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar
     </exists>
    </file>
   </activation>
   <properties>
    <toolsjar>
     ${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar
    </toolsjar>
   </properties>
  </profile>
  <profile>
   <id>
    mac-profile
   </id>
   <activation>
    <activeByDefault>
     false
    </activeByDefault>
    <file>
     <exists>
      ${java.home}/../Classes/classes.jar
     </exists>
    </file>
   </activation>
   <properties>
    <toolsjar>
     ${java.home}/../Classes/classes.jar
    </toolsjar>
   </properties>
  </profile>
 </profiles>
</project>

  <artifactId>auto-factory</artifactId>
  <version>1.0-SNAPSHOT</version>
  <name>AutoFactory</name>
  <description>
    JSR-330-compatible factories.
  </description>

  <scm>
    <url>http://github.com/google/auto</url>
    <connection>scm:git:git://github.com/google/auto.git</connection>
    <developerConnection>scm:git:ssh://git@github.com/google/auto.git</developerConnection>
    <tag>HEAD</tag>
  </scm>

    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.auto</groupId>
      <artifactId>auto-common</artifactId>
      <version>0.5</version>

      <artifactId>auto-service</artifactId>
      <version>1.0-rc2</version>
      <scope>provided</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.guava</groupId>
      <artifactId>guava</artifactId>
      <version>18.0</version>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.squareup</groupId>
      <artifactId>javawriter</artifactId>
      <version>2.5.1</version>

        </executions>
      </plugin>
    </plugins>
  </build>
</project>

BUILD ERROR ANALYSIS FOR GOOGLE AUTO PROJECT
==============================================

REPOSITORY: /home/travis/build/failed/google/auto
ERROR TYPE: Dependency Resolution Failure

ISSUE SUMMARY:
The build fails with: "Could not find artifact com.sun:tools:jar:11.0.27 at specified path /usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64/../lib/tools.jar"

ROOT CAUSE:
The OSS parent POM (version 7) defines a profile that attempts to include com.sun:tools as a dependency (pointing to the local JDK tools.jar file). This profile is activated when the file ${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar exists.

In Java 9+, the JDK structure changed and tools.jar no longer exists at the traditional location. Instead, the compiler tools are part of the standard modules. The profile activation mechanism in the oss-parent POM fails to find the expected file location.

AFFECTED MODULES:
- common (auto-common)
- factory (auto-factory)
- value (auto-value)
- service (auto-service)

The parent modules reference auto-parent version 3, which itself inherits from oss-parent version 7.

MAVEN CONFIGURATION ISSUE:
The profiles in oss-parent-7.pom are designed for Java 6-8 where tools.jar was part of the JDK distribution at ${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar. The build environment is running Java 11, which no longer provides this file structure.

SOLUTION APPROACH:
1. Add a "jdk9+" profile to the auto-parent or individual module POMs that disables the problematic tools.jar dependency for Java 9+
2. OR update the existing profiles to handle Java 9+ where tools.jar is not available
3. Configure Maven profiles to prevent activation of the default-profile when running on Java 9+

SPECIFIC FIXES NEEDED:
1. Disable the tools.jar dependency resolution for Java 9+ environments in each module that references it
2. Ensure the build profiles gracefully handle the absence of tools.jar on modern Java versions

Perfect! Now I found it. The compile-testing library has a hard dependency on com.sun:tools with system scope and systemPath. The fix needs to be applied to all modules' pom.xml files to either:
1. Override the toolsjar property for Java 9+
2. Exclude the tools dependency

Let me create more comprehensive patches. First, let me update my analysis file:

input.old_string:
BUILD ERROR ANALYSIS FOR GOOGLE AUTO PROJECT
==============================================

REPOSITORY: /home/travis/build/failed/google/auto
ERROR TYPE: Dependency Resolution Failure

ISSUE SUMMARY:
The build fails with: "Could not find artifact com.sun:tools:jar:11.0.27 at specified path /usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64/../lib/tools.jar"

ROOT CAUSE:
The OSS parent POM (version 7) defines a profile that attempts to include com.sun:tools as a dependency (pointing to the local JDK tools.jar file). This profile is activated when the file ${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar exists.

In Java 9+, the JDK structure changed and tools.jar no longer exists at the traditional location. Instead, the compiler tools are part of the standard modules. The profile activation mechanism in the oss-parent POM fails to find the expected file location.

AFFECTED MODULES:
- common (auto-common)
- factory (auto-factory)
- value (auto-value)
- service (auto-service)

The parent modules reference auto-parent version 3, which itself inherits from oss-parent version 7.

MAVEN CONFIGURATION ISSUE:
The profiles in oss-parent-7.pom are designed for Java 6-8 where tools.jar was part of the JDK distribution at ${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar. The build environment is running Java 11, which no longer provides this file structure.

SOLUTION APPROACH:
1. Add a "jdk9+" profile to the auto-parent or individual module POMs that disables the problematic tools.jar dependency for Java 9+
2. OR update the existing profiles to handle Java 9+ where tools.jar is not available
3. Configure Maven profiles to prevent activation of the default-profile when running on Java 9+

SPECIFIC FIXES NEEDED:
1. Disable the tools.jar dependency resolution for Java 9+ environments in each module that references it
2. Ensure the build profiles gracefully handle the absence of tools.jar on modern Java versions

ISSUE SUMMARY:
The build fails with: "Could not find artifact com.sun:tools:jar:11.0.27 at specified path /usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64/../lib/tools.jar"

ROOT CAUSE:
The build depends on com.google.testing.compile:compile-testing:0.7, which has a hard dependency on com.sun:tools with system scope and systemPath=${toolsjar}.

The compile-testing library and the parent POMs define profiles that set ${toolsjar} based on whether tools.jar exists at the traditional Java 6-8 locations:
- ${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar (default-profile, Linux)
- ${java.home}/../Classes/classes.jar (mac-profile, macOS)

In Java 9+, the JDK structure changed fundamentally. The tools.jar file no longer exists at these locations. Instead, the compiler tools are built-in modules. The build fails because:
1. The "default-profile" profile check fails to find ${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar
2. The "mac-profile" check also fails
3. Without a matching profile, ${toolsjar} remains undefined
4. Maven tries to resolve com.sun:tools at ${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar (literally the string, not expanded)
5. The artifact cannot be found, causing the build to fail

AFFECTED MODULES:
- common (auto-common) - depends on compile-testing:0.7
- factory (auto-factory) - depends on compile-testing:0.8
- value (auto-value) - depends on compile-testing:0.6
- service (auto-service) - likely depends on compile-testing

DEPENDENCY CHAIN:
com.google.testing.compile:compile-testing:0.7 -> com.sun:tools:${java.version}:system:${toolsjar}

MAVEN CONFIGURATION ISSUE:
The profiles are designed for Java 6-8. On Java 9+, neither profile activation condition is met, leaving ${toolsjar} undefined.

SOLUTION:
Add two new profiles to all affected modules:
1. "java9-profile" - activated by JDK version [9,) that sets ${toolsjar} to empty string
2. "no-tools-jar" - activated when ${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar is missing, that sets ${toolsjar} to empty string

These profiles ensure ${toolsjar} is always defined, preventing Maven from trying to literally interpret the path.

The real solution is to need to exclude the com.sun:tools dependency from compile-testing. Let me take a different approach - exclude the tools dependency:

BUILD ERROR ANALYSIS FOR GOOGLE AUTO PROJECT
==============================================

REPOSITORY: /home/travis/build/failed/google/auto
ERROR TYPE: Dependency Resolution Failure

ISSUE SUMMARY:
The build fails with: "Could not find artifact com.sun:tools:jar:11.0.27 at specified path /usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64/../lib/tools.jar"

ROOT CAUSE:
The build depends on com.google.testing.compile:compile-testing:0.7, which has a hard dependency on com.sun:tools with system scope and systemPath=${toolsjar}.

The compile-testing library and the parent POMs define profiles that set ${toolsjar} based on whether tools.jar exists at the traditional Java 6-8 locations:
- ${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar (default-profile, Linux)
- ${java.home}/../Classes/classes.jar (mac-profile, macOS)

In Java 9+, the JDK structure changed fundamentally. The tools.jar file no longer exists at these locations. Instead, the compiler tools are built-in modules. The build fails because:
1. The "default-profile" profile check fails to find ${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar
2. The "mac-profile" check also fails
3. Without a matching profile, ${toolsjar} remains undefined
4. Maven tries to resolve com.sun:tools at ${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar (literally the string, not expanded)
5. The artifact cannot be found, causing the build to fail

AFFECTED MODULES:
- common (auto-common) - depends on compile-testing:0.7
- factory (auto-factory) - depends on compile-testing:0.8
- value (auto-value) - depends on compile-testing:0.6
- service (auto-service) - likely depends on compile-testing

DEPENDENCY CHAIN:
com.google.testing.compile:compile-testing:0.7 -> com.sun:tools:${java.version}:system:${toolsjar}

MAVEN CONFIGURATION ISSUE:
The profiles are designed for Java 6-8. On Java 9+, neither profile activation condition is met, leaving ${toolsjar} undefined.

SOLUTION:
Add two new profiles to all affected modules:
1. "java9-profile" - activated by JDK version [9,) that sets ${toolsjar} to empty string
2. "no-tools-jar" - activated when ${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar is missing, that sets ${toolsjar} to empty string

These profiles ensure ${toolsjar} is always defined, preventing Maven from trying to literally interpret the path.

BUILD ERROR ANALYSIS FOR GOOGLE AUTO PROJECT
==============================================

REPOSITORY: /home/travis/build/failed/google/auto
ERROR TYPE: Dependency Resolution Failure

ISSUE SUMMARY:
The build fails with: "Could not find artifact com.sun:tools:jar:11.0.27 at specified path /usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64/../lib/tools.jar"

ROOT CAUSE:
The build depends on com.google.testing.compile:compile-testing:0.7, which has a hard dependency on com.sun:tools with system scope and systemPath=${toolsjar}.

The compile-testing library and the parent POMs define profiles that set ${toolsjar} based on whether tools.jar exists at the traditional Java 6-8 locations:
- ${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar (default-profile, Linux)
- ${java.home}/../Classes/classes.jar (mac-profile, macOS)

In Java 9+, the JDK structure changed fundamentally. The tools.jar file no longer exists at these locations. Instead, the compiler tools are built-in modules. The build fails because:
1. The "default-profile" profile check fails to find ${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar
2. The "mac-profile" check also fails
3. Without a matching profile, ${toolsjar} remains undefined
4. Maven tries to resolve com.sun:tools at ${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar (literally the string, not expanded)
5. The artifact cannot be found, causing the build to fail

AFFECTED MODULES:
- common (auto-common) - depends on compile-testing:0.7
- factory (auto-factory) - depends on compile-testing:0.8
- value (auto-value) - depends on compile-testing:0.6
- service (auto-service) - likely depends on compile-testing

DEPENDENCY CHAIN:
com.google.testing.compile:compile-testing:0.7 -> com.sun:tools:${java.version}:system:${toolsjar}

MAVEN CONFIGURATION ISSUE:
The profiles are designed for Java 6-8. On Java 9+, neither profile activation condition is met, leaving ${toolsjar} undefined.

SOLUTION:
Add two new profiles to all affected modules:
1. "java9-profile" - activated by JDK version [9,) that sets ${toolsjar} to empty string
2. "no-tools-jar" - activated when ${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar is missing, that sets ${toolsjar} to empty string

These profiles ensure ${toolsjar} is always defined, preventing Maven from trying to literally interpret the path.
